exercises.title: Bài 1 · The components of an information system
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
An information system (IS) is an organised combination of people, hardware, software, networks, data and procedures that collects, processes, stores and distributes information to support decision-making and control in an organisation. These six components work together: hardware and software process the data, networks transmit it, and people follow procedures to use the results.

Every IS follows the input–processing–output cycle. Input is raw data, for example a customer's order entered at a till. Processing converts data into information by sorting, calculating and summarising it. Output is delivered to users as reports or dashboards, and feedback allows managers to compare the results with the goals and adjust the system. Some systems use real-time processing, while others handle transactions in batches at night.

Different management levels need different systems. A transaction processing system (TPS) supports operational staff by recording daily events. A management information system (MIS) turns this data into regular reports for tactical managers, a decision support system (DSS) helps with non-routine problems, and an executive information system (EIS) gives strategic summaries to senior leaders. Together, these systems improve efficiency and accuracy, and they can create a lasting competitive advantage.

content.q: An information system consists of hardware and software only.
content.why: Đoạn 1: IS gồm **sáu thành phần**: con người, phần cứng, phần mềm, mạng, dữ liệu và quy trình.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Case study: Replacing a legacy system at a regional bank
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A regional bank with 120 branches relied on a legacy core banking system developed in the 1990s. Although it was reliable, it was expensive to maintain and could not support mobile payments. Customer data was stored in separate files, so the same client sometimes appeared with different addresses, which reduced data accuracy.

The CIO appointed a business analyst to interview stakeholders in each department. The analyst discovered that tellers were spending much of their time on manual data entry, and that managers were waiting days for monthly reports. The bank therefore decided to adopt a modern transaction processing system with a central database and a management dashboard.

During the first phase, batch processing was replaced by real-time processing for card payments. Branch managers now monitor key figures on dashboards instead of waiting for printed reports. Although the migration is still continuing, early results show faster transactions, fewer errors and higher customer satisfaction. The CIO stresses that the technology is only one part of the project; training end users and redesigning procedures are equally important.

content.why: Đoạn 1: hệ thống lõi được phát triển từ thập niên 1990.

content.q: Customer data was stored in one central database.
content.why: Đoạn 1: dữ liệu khách hàng nằm trong **các tệp riêng biệt**.

content.why: Đoạn 2: giao dịch viên mất nhiều thời gian nhập liệu thủ công.

content.q: Why was the legacy system a problem?
content.why: Đoạn 1: tốn kém bảo trì và không hỗ trợ thanh toán di động.
opts: It was expensive and could not support mobile payments

content.why: Đoạn 2: CIO giao chuyên viên phỏng vấn các bên liên quan.

content.q: What replaced batch processing for card payments?
content.why: Đoạn 3: xử lý thời gian thực thay thế xử lý theo lô.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · ERP: integrating the enterprise
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems integrate the core processes of an organisation—finance, human resources, production, inventory and sales—in a single software platform with a shared database. The main advantage is a single source of truth: when a sales order is entered, the inventory module, the accounting module and the production schedule are updated automatically. This is more accurate and much faster than re-entering the same data in separate applications.

Two typical end-to-end processes illustrate this integration. In order-to-cash, a customer order triggers stock checking, delivery, invoicing and payment collection. In procure-to-pay, a purchase request leads to a purchase order, goods receipt, supplier invoice and payment. Because each step creates an audit trail, managers and auditors can follow every transaction from beginning to end.

However, ERP projects are more demanding than most IT projects. Companies must choose between on-premise and cloud-based deployment, estimate the total cost of ownership and decide how much customization they need. Heavy customization makes upgrades harder and more expensive, so many experts recommend using standard configuration wherever possible. Studies of failed implementations show that poor change management, rather than technical problems, is the most common cause.

content.why: Đoạn 1: ERP dùng một cơ sở dữ liệu dùng chung.

content.q: In an ERP, entering a sales order updates only the sales module.
content.why: Đoạn 1: kho, kế toán và lịch sản xuất **cũng** được cập nhật tự động.

content.q: Order-to-cash begins with a customer order.
content.why: Đoạn 2: đơn hàng của khách kích hoạt quy trình order-to-cash.

content.q: Heavy customization makes upgrades easier.
content.why: Đoạn 3: tùy biến nhiều làm nâng cấp **khó và đắt hơn**.

content.q: What is the main advantage of ERP according to the text?
content.why: Đoạn 1: lợi ích chính là nguồn dữ liệu thống nhất.

content.q: What does an audit trail allow?
content.why: Đoạn 2: người quản lý và kiểm toán truy vết từng giao dịch.
opts: Following every transaction from beginning to end

content.q: Why do many experts recommend standard configuration?
content.why: Đoạn 3: tùy biến nặng khiến nâng cấp khó và tốn kém.
opts: It removes the need for a vendor
It is the only legal option
Heavy customization makes upgrades harder and more expensive

content.q: What is the most common cause of failed ERP implementations?
content.why: Đoạn 3: quản lý thay đổi kém, không phải lỗi kỹ thuật.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Case study: A manufacturer implements ERP and CRM
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A furniture manufacturer with three factories used separate programs for accounting, stock and sales. The result was costly: production managers could not see current stock levels, and sales staff often promised delivery dates that the factories could not meet. Because the bill of materials was stored in a spreadsheet, material costs were calculated incorrectly.

The company selected a cloud-based ERP from an international vendor and a separate CRM, integrated through standard interfaces. The project team prepared master data, migrated historical records and configured the workflows for order-to-cash and procure-to-pay. They chose not to customize the core modules, since the vendor's standard processes were close to the company's needs.

Six months after go-live, forecasting accuracy has improved and inventory levels have fallen by 18 percent. The sales pipeline in the CRM now shows realistic delivery dates because it is connected to production planning. The project manager admits that the first two months were difficult: users had been trained too late, and some data had been migrated with errors. The lesson learned was that user training and data quality must start earlier than the technical work.

content.q: The manufacturer has three factories.
content.why: Đoạn 1: nhà sản xuất có ba nhà máy.

content.q: The company customized all the core ERP modules.
content.why: Đoạn 2: họ **chọn không** tùy biến các phân hệ lõi.

content.q: Inventory levels fell by 18 percent.
content.why: Đoạn 3: tồn kho giảm 18%.

content.q: Users were trained too early.
content.why: Đoạn 3: người dùng được đào tạo **quá muộn**.

content.q: What problem did production managers have before ERP?
content.why: Đoạn 1: họ không thấy mức tồn kho hiện tại.
opts: They could not see current stock levels

content.q: How were the ERP and CRM connected?
content.why: Đoạn 2: tích hợp qua các giao diện chuẩn.

content.q: Why did the company not customize the core modules?
content.why: Đoạn 2: quy trình chuẩn của nhà cung cấp gần với nhu cầu.
opts: The vendor's standard processes were close to its needs

content.q: What was the lesson learned?
content.why: Đoạn 3: đào tạo và chất lượng dữ liệu phải bắt đầu sớm hơn công việc kỹ thuật.
opts: Training and data quality must start earlier than technical work

exercises.title: Bài 1 · From operational data to business intelligence
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Organisations generate data in operational systems, such as ordering, billing and customer service. These systems are based on OLTP databases, which are optimised for fast, short transactions and are designed with normalised tables to avoid data redundancy. However, a normalised OLTP database is not suitable for analysis, because complex queries across many tables are slow and may disturb daily operations.

For this reason, data is periodically extracted from the source systems, transformed and loaded into a data warehouse through an ETL process. During transformation, data is cleansed, duplicates are removed and codes are standardised, so that the warehouse becomes a consistent record of the organisation's history. Smaller data marts are often created for individual departments, while a data lake is used to store large volumes of unstructured data such as emails, images and sensor readings.

On top of the warehouse, business intelligence tools provide OLAP analysis, dashboards and data visualization. Users can drill down from a summary to the underlying transactions and monitor KPIs without waiting for the IT department. A mature organisation also applies data governance: policies define who owns the data, how quality is measured and how long it is retained.

content.q: OLTP databases are optimised for fast, short transactions.
content.why: Đoạn 1: OLTP tối ưu cho giao dịch ngắn và nhanh.

content.q: Complex analytical queries are fast on normalised OLTP tables.
content.why: Đoạn 1: truy vấn phức tạp trên nhiều bảng **chậm** và có thể gây gián đoạn.

content.q: A data lake is used to store large volumes of unstructured data.
content.why: Đoạn 2: hồ dữ liệu lưu dữ liệu phi cấu trúc khối lượng lớn.

content.q: Data governance defines only the colours of dashboards.
content.why: Đoạn 3: quản trị dữ liệu xác định **ai sở hữu, đo chất lượng thế nào, lưu bao lâu**.

Warehouses are cheaper than any other database

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Case study: A retail chain builds a single customer view
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A retail chain with 200 stores and an online shop had customer data in four systems: point-of-sale, e-commerce, loyalty cards and customer service. The same customer was often recorded several times with slightly different names, and marketing campaigns were therefore sent twice to the same person. A data quality assessment found that about 15 percent of customer records were duplicates.

A data governance committee was established, and a data steward was appointed for each domain. Master data management software was introduced to match and merge records, and an ETL pipeline was built to load the cleaned data into a central warehouse every night. Unstructured data, such as customer reviews and call recordings, was stored in a data lake and analysed by a data scientist.

As a result, a single customer view is now available to store managers and call-centre staff. Predictive analytics has been used to identify customers who are likely to leave, and personalised offers are sent to them. Retention of personal data is controlled by a retention policy, and privacy rules are applied in accordance with the law. The chain reports a 9 percent increase in repeat purchases, although managers warn that data quality must be monitored continuously.

content.why: Đoạn 1: khoảng 15% hồ sơ bị trùng.

content.why: Đoạn 2: khớp và gộp các bản ghi.

content.why: Đoạn 2: dữ liệu phi cấu trúc lưu trong hồ dữ liệu.

content.q: How is predictive analytics used?
content.why: Đoạn 3: nhận diện khách hàng có nguy cơ rời đi.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Requirements: the foundation of system design
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Systems analysis begins with a clear understanding of the problem. After a feasibility study has confirmed that the project is worthwhile, analysts must elicit requirements from stakeholders. Several techniques are used: stakeholder interviews give detailed opinions, questionnaires reach many users quickly, and observation shows how work is really done, which people often cannot describe accurately.

Requirements are normally divided into functional requirements, which describe what the system must do, and non-functional requirements, which define qualities such as performance, security and usability. Each requirement has to be unambiguous, testable and traceable to a business goal. Analysts record them in a requirements specification, often supported by use cases and user stories, and every change must go through a formal change request so that scope creep is controlled.

In the design phase, models make the requirements concrete. Data flow diagrams show how data moves between processes, class diagrams describe the structure of the data and sequence diagrams show interactions over time. Wireframes and prototypes let users see the interface early, which is cheaper than correcting misunderstandings after programming. Finally, validation confirms that the right system is being built, whereas verification confirms that it is being built correctly.

content.q: Observation shows how work is really done.
content.why: Đoạn 1: quan sát cho thấy công việc thực sự diễn ra thế nào.

content.q: Non-functional requirements describe what the system must do.

content.q: Verification confirms that the right system is being built.
content.why: Đoạn 3: đó là **validation**; verification kiểm tra hệ thống được xây **đúng cách**.

content.q: Why is observation useful?
content.why: Đoạn 1: người ta thường không mô tả chính xác cách họ thực sự làm việc.
opts: People often cannot describe how they really work
It is the cheapest technique for every project

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Case study: Designing a hospital appointment system
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A public hospital wanted a new appointment system because patients were waiting up to two hours at the reception desk. A business analyst began with observation and interviews. She discovered that receptionists had to check three separate lists before booking an appointment, and that doctors' schedules were changed by telephone. These findings led to the main functional requirements: patients should be able to book online, doctors must be able to update their availability, and the system has to send reminders by text message.

The non-functional requirements were equally important. Because the system stores medical data, it must comply with privacy law and must use two-factor authentication. It also has to respond within two seconds even when 500 users are logged in. The analyst drew use cases for the actors Patient, Receptionist and Doctor, and created data flow diagrams to show how an appointment moves from request to confirmation.

A prototype of the booking screen was tested with ten patients. Several older users found the date picker confusing, so the design was simplified before development started. The project board signed off the specification after one change request, which added support for interpreters. During user acceptance testing, receptionists confirmed that waiting times had fallen to under fifteen minutes.

content.why: Đoạn 1: bệnh nhân chờ tới hai giờ.

content.q: Receptionists had to check only one list.
content.why: Đoạn 1: họ phải kiểm tra **ba danh sách** riêng.

content.why: Đoạn 2: hệ thống lưu dữ liệu y tế nên phải dùng xác thực hai yếu tố.

content.q: The prototype was tested with receptionists only.
content.why: Đoạn 3: bản mẫu được thử với **mười bệnh nhân**.

content.q: How were doctors' schedules changed before the project?
content.why: Đoạn 1: lịch bác sĩ được thay đổi qua điện thoại.

exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
The choice of development methodology strongly influences how an IS project is planned and controlled. In the waterfall model, the project moves through sequential phases—requirements, design, implementation, testing and maintenance—and each phase must be completed and signed off before the next one begins. If the requirements are stable and well understood, as in a regulated payroll system, waterfall offers predictability: the WBS, Gantt chart and critical path can be defined at the beginning, and progress is measured against the baseline.

Agile methods assume that requirements will change. In Scrum, the product owner maintains a prioritised product backlog, and the team delivers a potentially releasable increment in each sprint of two to four weeks. The scrum master removes obstacles, daily stand-ups keep everyone aligned, and a retrospective at the end of each sprint produces lessons learned. If users see working software early, they can correct misunderstandings before they become expensive. Kanban, by contrast, limits the amount of work in progress and suits maintenance teams with continuous requests.

Many organisations combine both approaches. A hybrid project might use waterfall for infrastructure and contracts, and Scrum for application development. Whatever the method, a risk register, a steering committee and regular status reports remain necessary, because methodology cannot replace sound project governance.

exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A ministry commissioned an online portal for business registration. The first plan used waterfall, with a fixed budget of 4 billion dong and delivery in eighteen months. After nine months, however, new regulations changed several requirements, and the project manager reported a cost overrun of 20 percent and a three-month schedule delay. The steering committee decided that if the project continued in the same way, the portal would be obsolete on the day it was launched.

The team therefore switched to a hybrid approach. The contract and infrastructure remained under waterfall control, but the application was rebuilt in Scrum sprints of three weeks. The product owner, a senior official, ranked the backlog by business value, and a minimum viable product containing only company registration was released after four months. Citizens' feedback was collected through a short survey, and the retrospective showed that the form was too long. The next increment shortened it by half.

Continuous integration and automated QA reduced the number of defects that reached production. A contingency plan for the registration peak before the tax deadline, which included extra servers, was tested in advance. At the final review, the sponsor noted that if the ministry had insisted on the original plan, it would have spent more and received less. The main lesson learned was to involve users early and to deliver value in small, working increments.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · From data centers to the cloud
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Traditionally, organisations ran their information systems in their own data centers. Each application ran on a dedicated server, which was often idle most of the time, and capacity had to be planned for the busiest day of the year. Virtualization changed this model: a hypervisor allows many virtual machines to share one physical server, which increases utilisation and simplifies backup and disaster recovery.

Cloud computing extended the idea. Providers deliver computing as a service over the internet, and customers pay only for what they use. In the IaaS model, the customer rents virtual machines and storage; in PaaS, the provider also manages the operating system and runtime; in SaaS, the customer simply uses the application. Elasticity means that resources can grow or shrink automatically with demand, which is particularly valuable for seasonal businesses. Public clouds are shared by many customers, private clouds are dedicated to one organisation, and a hybrid cloud combines both.

Nevertheless, cloud adoption creates new risks. Latency can be a problem for real-time applications, which is why edge computing is growing. Vendor lock-in may make it expensive to change provider, and the service level agreement must clearly define uptime, support and the recovery time objective. Finally, the energy consumption of large data centers has led many organisations to adopt green IT policies.

exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
In 2019, a mid-sized bank decided to modernise its IT infrastructure. Its two data centers, built in the early 2000s, had suffered several outages, and peak transaction volumes during the Lunar New Year holiday had repeatedly slowed the online banking service. The IT department calculated that it would need to buy forty new servers just to cover that single peak.

Instead, the bank adopted a hybrid cloud. Customer databases and core banking remained in a private cloud for regulatory reasons, while the mobile app and the analytics platform were moved to a public cloud. The architects containerised the app into microservices and placed a load balancer in front of them, so that capacity increases automatically. A redundant WAN link and a failover site were installed, and the disaster recovery plan set a recovery time objective of one hour and a recovery point objective of five minutes.

The results have been positive. Since the migration, the bank has recorded 99.98 percent uptime, and last year's holiday peak caused no outage. Infrastructure costs fell by 14 percent, although the bank has also faced new challenges: cloud bills are less predictable, and the team has had to learn to avoid vendor lock-in by using open standards. The CIO has said that capacity planning is now a continuous task, not an annual one.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · The CIA triad and risk management
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Information security aims to protect three properties of information that are known as the CIA triad. Confidentiality means that data is accessible only to people who are authorised to see it; integrity means that data is accurate and has not been altered without permission; availability means that systems and data can be used whenever they are needed. A ransomware attack, which encrypts files and demands a ransom, damages availability, while an unauthorised change to a bank balance damages integrity.

Security management is based on risk. In a risk assessment, the organisation identifies its assets, the threats that could harm them and the vulnerabilities that threats can exploit. Risk is then estimated as a combination of likelihood and impact, and countermeasures are selected to reduce the highest risks. These controls may be technical, such as firewalls, encryption and multi-factor authentication; organisational, such as the segregation of duties and the principle of least privilege; or physical, such as locked server rooms. Access control, which combines authentication and authorization, ensures that users can do only what their role requires.

No control is perfect, so organisations also prepare for failure. An incident response plan defines who must react when a breach is detected, and a business continuity plan makes sure that critical processes can continue. Regular security audits and penetration tests, which are carried out by independent specialists, reveal weaknesses before criminals find them. Finally, the human factor matters: social engineering, which exploits trust rather than technology, can bypass the best technical defences, so staff awareness training is essential.

content.q: Ransomware mainly damages availability.
content.why: Đoạn 1: mã độc tống tiền mã hóa tệp và làm mất tính sẵn sàng.

content.q: Risk is estimated as a combination of likelihood and impact.

opts: Data is accurate and not altered without permission

content.why: Đoạn 3: xác định ai phải phản ứng khi phát hiện xâm phạm.
opts: To increase the likelihood of attacks

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Case study: A data breach at an online insurer
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
An online insurer, whose systems stored the personal data of 800,000 customers, discovered unusual database queries one Friday evening. The intrusion detection system, which had been configured only a month earlier, raised an alert, and the incident response team, which consisted of five specialists, isolated the affected servers within forty minutes.

The investigation showed that an attacker had sent a phishing email to a claims officer, who had entered her password on a fake login page. The account, which had broad access rights and no multi-factor authentication, allowed the attacker to reach the customer database. This violated the principle of least privilege, and a security audit later found that two other accounts that belonged to former employees were still active.

The insurer, which is subject to GDPR, notified the regulator and the affected customers within seventy-two hours. It introduced MFA for all staff, replaced broad permissions with role-based access control, and began a quarterly access review. The business continuity plan, which had been tested only on paper, worked less well than expected; the online claims portal was unavailable for nine hours. The CIO admitted that the weakest link had been the human factor, and that technical controls which are not supported by training and governance rarely succeed.

content.q: The intrusion detection system raised an alert.
content.why: Đoạn 1: IDS phát cảnh báo.

content.q: The affected servers were isolated after two days.
content.why: Đoạn 1: máy chủ bị cô lập trong **bốn mươi phút**.

content.q: The attacker used a phishing email.
content.why: Đoạn 2: kẻ tấn công gửi email lừa đảo cho nhân viên bồi thường.

content.q: The claims portal remained available throughout.
content.why: Đoạn 3: cổng bồi thường **không khả dụng chín giờ**.

content.q: What did the claims officer do?
content.why: Đoạn 2: nhập mật khẩu vào trang đăng nhập giả.
opts: Sent the customer list to the regulator
Entered her password on a fake login page

content.q: Which principle was violated?
content.why: Đoạn 2: tài khoản có quyền quá rộng, vi phạm đặc quyền tối thiểu.

content.q: What did the insurer introduce after the breach?
content.why: Đoạn 3: MFA cho toàn bộ nhân viên và kiểm soát truy cập theo vai trò.
opts: MFA for all staff and role-based access control

content.q: What was the CIO's conclusion?
content.why: Đoạn 3: mắt xích yếu nhất là yếu tố con người.
opts: The weakest link was the human factor

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Digital transformation: more than technology
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Digital transformation is often misunderstood as the purchase of new software. In fact, it is a fundamental change in how an organisation creates value, and technology is only one of its elements. Researchers distinguish digitization, the conversion of analogue information into digital form, from digitalization, the redesign of processes to exploit digital data, and from digital transformation, which also changes the business model, the culture and the relationship with customers.

The technologies that drive this change are well known. Cloud-native architectures and APIs allow companies to connect with partners and form ecosystems; big data analytics supports data-driven decisions; RPA and AI automate routine work, and the Internet of Things generates streams of sensor data. As a result, new platform businesses have disrupted traditional industries such as retail, banking and transport. Nevertheless, most transformation programmes fail to reach their goals, mainly because of organisational factors: change resistance, weak leadership and a lack of digital literacy.

Successful organisations therefore treat transformation as a continuous journey. They start from the customer experience, modernise legacy systems gradually, use low-code platforms to empower business users, and measure the return on digital investment with clear KPIs. Although technology changes quickly, the ability to learn and adapt remains the most important competitive advantage.

content.why: Đoạn 1: digitization = chuyển thông tin tương tự sang dạng số.

content.q: Digital transformation means only buying new software.
content.why: Đoạn 1: nó là **thay đổi căn bản** cách tổ chức tạo ra giá trị.

content.q: Platform businesses have disrupted industries such as retail and banking.

content.q: Most transformation programmes fail mainly because of technical problems.
content.why: Đoạn 2: nguyên nhân chính là **yếu tố tổ chức** như kháng cự thay đổi.

opts: Because of organisational factors such as change resistance

content.q: What remains the most important competitive advantage?

exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A regional logistics company with 600 trucks was losing customers to digital competitors. Although its drivers were experienced, delivery times were unpredictable because routes were planned by hand. The management therefore launched a digital transformation programme under a new chief digital officer.

First, sensors and GPS devices were installed in every truck, so that the company could collect real-time data about location, fuel consumption and engine condition. A cloud-native platform processed this data, and machine learning models predicted delays and maintenance needs. As a result, unplanned breakdowns fell by 35 percent. A digital twin of the main warehouse was used to test new layouts before they were built, which saved several weeks of work.

However, the programme did not run smoothly. Some drivers resisted the change because they feared constant monitoring; consequently, the company organised workshops about data privacy and algorithmic bias, and it agreed that the data would be used for safety, not punishment. Customers now use an app with live tracking and a chatbot, and an API allows large clients to connect their own systems. Despite initial costs of several billion dong, the return on digital investment has been positive after only two years, and the company has begun to offer its platform to smaller carriers.

content.why: Đoạn 1: công ty có 600 xe tải.

content.q: Delivery times were predictable because routes were planned by hand.
content.why: Đoạn 1: thời gian giao **không thể dự đoán** vì lập tuyến thủ công.

content.q: Unplanned breakdowns fell by 35 percent.
content.why: Đoạn 2: hỏng hóc ngoài kế hoạch giảm 35%.

content.q: The company used the data to punish drivers.
content.why: Đoạn 3: dữ liệu được dùng cho **an toàn, không phải trừng phạt**.

content.why: Đoạn 2: cảm biến và thiết bị GPS.

content.why: Đoạn 2: thử bố trí kho mới trước khi xây dựng.
